svg.aria-label: nes-bench bridge v1b: the UNO version, one supply, one port (sheet 1 of 2: the console side)

g.text: nes-bench bridge v1b: the UNO version, one supply, one port (sheet 1 of 2: the console side)
the ATmega328 is a 5 V part, so the register, the pad and the console share one domain. 2026-09-08. Not built; pulse widths authored until B0.

svg.text: THE CONSOLE PORT, THE INVERTER AND THE REGISTER, ALL AT +5V
DECOUPLING, AND WHAT THE CONSOLE ACTUALLY DOES
MEASURED 2026-09-09: supply on 5, 6 and 7 not carried; pin 5 not used here
2.0 V threshold: safe on NMOS OUT0
one 100nF across each of U1, U2 and U3,
at the chip's own supply pins
OUT0 high: U1 drives /PL low and the 165 loads its eight inputs. It is transparent while low,
so the byte must already be in U3 (sheet 2). OUT0 falls, /PL goes high, the byte is held, and
QH shows A. Each CLK rising edge shifts the next bit out: B, Select, Start, Up, Down, Left,
Right, then DS = GND, so the ninth read and later return 1 as an original pad does.
Pressed is LOW, which is what the pad's own 4021 drives.
MEASURED 2026-09-15: a lone pressed bit from B to Left showed on D0 for 50 ns and the
register read as if shifted once too often; D0's own falling edge was re-clocking the 165.
R2 and C4 (100 ns) sit at pin 2 against a spike that short; the console's clock is
microseconds wide and passes. The UNO's D2 still counts CON_CLK ahead of R2.
